claims.statement: ecshopx-bootstrap runs on Undertow (spring-boot-starter-tomcat excluded, spring-boot-starter-undertow added) and sets PHP-compatibility edge options in application.properties: server.undertow.options.server.allow-unescaped-characters-in-url=true (raw UTF-8 query bytes), server.undertow.max-http-post-size=64MB (kept above spring.servlet.multipart.max-file-size=50MB / max-request-size=55MB), and spring.mvc.servlet.pathmatch.use-trailing-slash-match=true (collection URLs match with or without trailing slash).

UndertowMultipartMaxEntityCustomizer is a WebServerFactoryCustomizer for UndertowServletWebServerFactory that raises UndertowOptions.MULTIPART_MAX_ENTITY_SIZE to 64MB — because Undertow 2.3+ enforces a separate multipart entity cap (near 2MB) independent of spring.servlet.multipart.* — and enables UndertowOptions.ALLOW_ENCODED_SLASH so encoded %2F reaches servlet mapping.

StrictHttpFirewallConfig installs StorageAwareHttpFirewall as the Spring Security HttpFirewall via a WebSecurityCustomizer; the firewall routes /storage/** (and exact /storage) through the lenient DefaultHttpFirewall so local image URLs with Chinese/mojibake non-ASCII filenames are not rejected, while all other paths use StrictHttpFirewall with relaxations for encoded slash, encoded double slash, and semicolons. StorageUnicodeHttpFirewallTest pins that /storage/** with Chinese passes and non-storage Chinese paths are still rejected.

/storage/** is served as static resources by StorageWebMvcConfigurer in ecshopx-espier only when ecshopx.storage.driver=local (default), mapping the ecshopx.storage.local.root (default storage/app/public) directory onto the /storage/** resource handler.

EspierSecurityConfig keeps Spring Security thin: a wxappMemberSessionSecurityFilterChain (Order -2, matcher /api/v1/wxapp/**) that authenticates every request by inserting WxappMemberSessionAuthenticationFilter before UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter, and a defaultPermitAllSecurityFilterChain (Order 100, matcher /api/**) with everything permitted; authorization has moved to annotations plus interceptors.

WxappMemberSessionAuthenticationFilter authenticates /api/v1/wxapp/** requests from the x-wxapp-session header via WxappMemberAuthService, stores the auth map under the WxappMemberAuthAttributes.REQUEST_ATTR request attribute and a UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken in the SecurityContext, and writes auth failures as a Dingo-style nested-data envelope with HTTP 200 (data.message + data.status_code 400 or 401).

OperatorJwtAuthenticationFilter is a @Component OncePerRequestFilter (servlet-filter auto-registration, all URLs) acting as an operator-JWT safety net: it requires a valid admin Bearer JWT for every request that maps to a controller method and is not on its shouldNotFilter allowlist (unmapped paths fall through to 404/405 via RequestMappingHandlerMapping lookup; anonymous admin login/code/callback paths; /api/openapi/**; /wechatAuth/**; and the front surfaces /api/v1/h5app/** and /api/v1/wxapp/**). On success it verifies the HS256 token, checks exp and the operator JWT blacklist, enriches shop-app member tokens, runs CompanysActivationService.checkUserAuth, attaches the selected distributor for operator_type=distributor, and stores the claims map under OperatorJwtRequestAttributes.OPERATOR_JWT_USER_DATA.

MiddlewareWebMvcConfigurer in ecshopx-espier registers the MVC interceptor chain on /api/** in a fixed order: EspierAgreementRateLimitInterceptor (order 5, only /api/v1/espier/system/agreement), AdminAuthInterceptor (order 10, with the admin anonymous excludes), FrontNoAuthInterceptor (15), FrontAuthInterceptor (20), ActivatedInterceptor (100), DataPassInterceptor (200), ShopLogInterceptor (300). Every interceptor skips requests whose handler is not a HandlerMethod or lacks its annotation (method level first, then class level), making the chain annotation-routed.

FrontAuthInterceptor implements @FrontAuth: it verifies the H5 Bearer JWT via H5BearerJwtClaimsService (HS256 signature, issuer, time claims with leeway, required claims iss/iat/exp/nbf/sub/jti, positive company_id claim, H5 JWT blacklist), rejects with HTTP 401 and Dingo envelope code 401001 message 'Unable to authenticate user.' on failure, rejects a truthy disabled claim with HTTP 403 code 403001, and on success sets the h5AuthClaims and h5CompanyId request attributes. A method-level @FrontNoAuth suppresses the check even when the class carries @FrontAuth.

FrontNoAuthInterceptor implements @FrontNoAuth by always producing a company_id: first from a valid H5 Bearer JWT (enriched by H5JwtUserLoginInfoEnrichService plus a member-mobile backfill), otherwise anonymously from the appid parameter / authorizer-appid header (WeChat mapper or AliMiniAppCompanyIdLookupPort), then the fixed system company (common.system-companys-id when not SaaS, common.system-main-companys-id when SaaS), then the company_id query parameter, then the Origin domain via CompanyDomainLookupService; unresolved requests throw UnauthorizedException, except MembersController.getNoAuthDecryptPhoneNumber which passes with company_id 0. Anonymous requests get a synthetic claims map in h5AuthClaims.

FrontNoAuthInterceptor writes its 401 error in a Dingo nested-data envelope only when the handler carries @DingoResponse(unauthorized = true) — mapping the message '该账号已被禁用.' to code 401002 and everything else to 'Unable to authenticate user.' code 401001 — and otherwise writes plain ApiResult.fail(401, msg); this mirrors GlobalExceptionHandler's choice for the same annotation.

AdminAuthInterceptor implements @AdminAuth for operator-console endpoints: it requires a Bearer token, verifies it with OperatorJwtCompactCodec (own HMAC check with a jjwt legacy fallback), checks exp, enriches shop-app member tokens, runs CompanysActivationService.checkUserAuth (which validates the encrypted session token inside the id claim unless operator_type is shopadmin/user), attaches the operator id and the selected distributor for operator_type=distributor, and stores the claims map under the OPERATOR_JWT_USER_DATA attribute. It rejects 401 with a Dingo envelope (data.message + data.status_code, no code key) and 403 with ApiResult.fail(403, msg).

FrontMerchantAuthInterceptor (registered by MerchantInterceptorWebMvcConfigurer at order 25 on /api/**) implements @FrontMerchantAuth for merchant-settlement Mini Program endpoints: it verifies a separate merchant JWT under ecshopx.merchant.wxapp.jwt.* properties (issuer ecshopx, secret from JWT_SECRET, 60-minute default TTL) with HS256/issuer/time-claim checks and positive company_id/account_id claims, then confirms a MerchantSettlementApply row exists for account_id in the same company, exposing a MerchantWxappAuthAttributes(companyId, accountId) record as the request attribute; failures return the Dingo 401001 envelope.

QywxSalespersonAuthInterceptor (registered by SalespersonWebMvcConfigurer at order 21 on /api/**) implements @QywxSalespersonAuth for the Work-WeChat salesperson Mini Program: it authenticates the x-wxapp-session header against WxappSalespersonSessionAuthService (Redis frontSession3rd:<session> plus DB re-validation) and stores the auth map under QywxSalespersonAuthAttributes.REQUEST_ATTR; BadRequestException/UnauthorizedException/ForbiddenException become Dingo-style envelopes with business codes 400001/401001/403001 at the matching HTTP status.

ActivatedInterceptor (order 100) implements @Activated(routeAlias) by delegating to ActivatedMiddlewareService, which checks the route alias against the operator's role menus (ShopMenuService.collectApisFromMenus with menu version per operator type: distributor 3, dealer 5, merchant 6, supplier 7, else 1; admins skip unless common.check-superadmin-permission=true; fixed whitelist and delivery-staff paths bypass), verifies the company exists and is not disabled (assertShopOperatorCompanyActive), computes the distributor scope, and exposes distributor_id / distributorIds request attributes (ActivatedRequestAttributes) that FlexibleHttpServletParameterMap later merges into parameter maps. Failures throw ResourceException.

DataPassInterceptor (order 200) implements @DataPass (method-level, optional pathAlias defaulting to ClassSimpleName.methodName): for admin operators, merchant-main accounts, and self-delivery staff it is a no-op; otherwise, without datapass authorization it sets the request attribute x-datapass-block = 1 (controllers read it to mask sensitive data) and with authorization it inserts an OperatorDataPassLog row. It never blocks the request and swallows its own errors.

ShopLogInterceptor (order 300) implements @ShopLog in afterCompletion: for non-GET requests whose handler carries the annotation and whose OPERATOR_JWT_USER_DATA attribute is present, it writes a merchant operation log (log_type=operator, company/operator/merchant ids from the JWT claims, request URI, first X-Forwarded-For IP or remote address) through OperatorLogsWriteService, swallowing failures. @AdminLog is consumed by the AdminLogAspect AOP aspect instead, recording login audit logs when a 2xx ApiResult response contains a token.

@OperationLog is consumed by OperationLogAspect (AOP, ecshopx-common), which logs timed operation lines to the SLF4J logger named operation-log on method entry/return/throwing; it is not an MVC interceptor and no controller in the tree currently uses it — it is the reserved hook for future DB-backed operation logs.

FlexibleBodyWebMvcConfigurer (ecshopx-common, servlet web apps) prepends FlexibleBodyMethodArgumentResolver to the custom argument resolvers and configures a UrlPathHelper with setRemoveSemicolonContent(false) so semicolon path content survives handler mapping. FlexibleBody is the @RequestBody replacement that binds the same parameter from application/json, multipart/form-data, or application/x-www-form-urlencoded, dispatching by declared type (JsonNode, Map, or POJO via convertValue with a ServletRequestDataBinder fallback); required=false allows null/empty bodies while required=true throws BadRequestException('请求体不能为空') on empty, and @Valid triggers jakarta Validator checks converted to MethodArgumentNotValidException.

FlexibleHttpServletParameterMap.toObjectMap(request) converts the servlet parameter map into a PHP-style Map<String, Object>: bracket-array keys (name[]=) and repeated keys become Lists, indexed keys (name[0]=) fold into ordered Lists, nested bracket keys (rates[0][item_id]=) become nested maps/lists with all-numeric-key maps converted to index-ordered lists at any depth, and scalars stay Strings; it then injects the Activated middleware attributes distributor_id and distributorIds when the parameters do not already carry them, which is how admin endpoints become distributor-scoped.

The dominant front-controller idiom (WxappPaymentController.payment) merges FlexibleHttpServletParameterMap.toObjectMap(request) as the base map and putAll the @FlexibleBody(required = false) body map over it, so query/form parameters form the base and the parsed body wins on key conflicts — reproducing PHP/Laravel request-merge semantics; identity is then read from request attributes (wxapp session attr, then h5AuthClaims, backfilled from h5CompanyId and finally the merged params) rather than from parameters.

ApiResult is the standard success envelope: ApiResult.ok(data) renders {"code":200,"msg":"success","data":...} and ApiResult.fail(code,msg) renders {"code":code,"msg":msg} with data omitted via @JsonInclude(NON_NULL).

@DingoResponse (class or method) opts an endpoint into legacy PHP Dingo error envelopes with four knobs: resource() picks the ResourceException style (DINGO = dingoStyleError with embeddedStatusCode ?? 422 plus optional embeddedBusinessCode; DINGO_FIXED = fixed 422; PLAIN = standard ApiResult 422), badRequest() picks the BadRequestException style (NONE = ApiResult 400; DINGO_400/DINGO_422 = embedded ?? 400/422; DINGO_FIXED = fixed 422), unauthorized()/unauthorizedHttpOk() shape UnauthorizedException responses, and notFound() maps NoResourceFoundException to dingoStyleError("404 Not Found", 404). GlobalExceptionHandler resolves the annotation per request from the best-matching handler, so new endpoints need no handler routing-table change.

GlobalExceptionHandler produces three Dingo envelope families: dingoStyleError returns HTTP 200 with {"data":{"message":...,"code":<businessCode>,"status_code":...}} (code key only when a business code exists); dingoStyleErrorHttp returns an HTTP status equal to status_code (used for ForbiddenException 403, ConflictException 409, TooManyRequestsException 429 under the annotation); and fixed 401 shapes under unauthorized=true — message '该账号已被禁用.' → code 401002, the H5 blacklist message 'The token has been blacklisted' → 401 without a business code, otherwise 'Unable to authenticate user.' code 401001 — with unauthorizedHttpOk=true returning HTTP 200 and data.status_code 403. Without the annotation (or the relevant attribute off), every exception falls back to plain ApiResult at the HTTP status.

GlobalExceptionHandler never applies Dingo envelopes to framework exceptions: MethodArgumentNotValidException → 422 ApiResult with 'field: message' pairs joined by '; ' (covering @FlexibleBody @Valid failures), MissingServletRequestParameterException / MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException / HttpMessageNotReadableException → 400 ApiResult with Chinese messages, HttpRequestMethodNotSupportedException → 405, NoResourceFoundException → 404 '资源不存在' (unless notFound=true), and any other Exception → 500 '服务器内部错误' logged at error.

ResourceException and BadRequestException carry the business error metadata (embeddedStatusCode, embeddedBusinessCode, and fieldErrors as a Map of field to error-code list such as validation.required); GlobalExceptionHandler does not expand fieldErrors — instead module-level @RestControllerAdvice beans at HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE (OrdersFrontV1BadRequestFieldErrorsAdvice, SalespersonFrontV1BadRequestFieldErrorsAdvice) and controller-local @ExceptionHandler methods (pointsmall front ItemsController) render the data.errors validation envelope and return null to defer to GlobalExceptionHandler.

Locale resolution is a filter, not a Spring LocaleResolver: CommonWebLocaleAutoConfiguration registers CountryCodeLocaleFilter on /* at Ordered.LOWEST_PRECEDENCE - 50; the filter takes the country_code query parameter (falling back to the first Accept-Language tag), normalizes it through LangueProperties.resolveToSupportedTag against langue.list (six pinned tags) and langue.default-lang=zh-CN, converts it via RequestMessageLocale.toMessageLocale (with the deliberate en-CN → en-US mapping for the messages_en_US bundle), sets LocaleContextHolder for the request thread, and resets it after the chain. Downstream code reads the tag with RequestLangTag.current or clamps per-company with LanguageTagSupport/CompanyLanguageResolver.

EspierAgreementRateLimitInterceptor (order 5, only /api/v1/espier/system/agreement) throttles the anonymous install-agreement endpoint by client IP via Redis key espier:agreement:throttle:<ip> (30 requests per minute on the companys Redis template) and writes {"message":"Too Many Attempts.","status_code":429} with HTTP 429 when exceeded.

H5 JWT secrets and TTLs are wired from environment variables in application.properties: JWT_SECRET (Base64 of a 32-byte key, required — interceptors/filters fail fast when blank) feeds both ecshopx.h5.jwt.secret-base64 and ecshopx.merchant.wxapp.jwt.secret-base64; JWT_TTL (default 120) and JWT_REFRESH_TTL (default 20160) set the H5 JWT TTL and refresh window; both H5 and operator JWT blacklists are keyed by sha256 of the compact token in the Redis prism DB (h5_jwt_invalidate:* with a grace period, operator_jwt_invalidate:*).

Controller web-slice tests across the repo build standalone MockMvc with setCustomArgumentResolvers(new FlexibleBodyMethodArgumentResolver(objectMapper, null)) and inject the authenticated operator via requestAttr(OperatorJwtRequestAttributes.OPERATOR_JWT_USER_DATA, claimsMap) — the established pattern for testing a controller without booting the interceptor chain.
